stem: What is the primary conclusion regarding the relationship between exposure to sexual content online and adolescent behavior?

options.text: Exposure clearly causes adolescents to engage in sexual activity at an earlier age.
Research has proven that online content has no measurable impact on body image.
The research is inconclusive regarding whether exposure causes behavior or behavior leads to seeking content.
Online sexual content is the leading cause of the decline in adolescent birth rates.

explanation: Because the studies are cross-sectional, they can only show associations, not the direction of cause and effect.
rationale: Think about the limitations of cross-sectional research when trying to determine cause and effect.

optionExplanations.A: The research is cross-sectional, meaning causality cannot be determined—it is unclear if content causes behavior or vice versa.
optionExplanations.B: The lecture notes that associations have been found with body shame and decreased sexual assertiveness.
optionExplanations.C: Because the studies are cross-sectional, they can only show associations, not the direction of cause and effect.
optionExplanations.D: The decline in birth rates is attributed to effective contraception and education, not online media content.
